questions.q: Which membrane approach is especially adaptable to a roof with complex curved geometry such as a shell surface?
questions.ref: National Roofing Contractors Association (NRCA) Roofing Manual - roof membranes, underlayments and drainage terminology
questions.n: Fluid-applied membranes can conform continuously to complex or irregular roof geometry.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes Pratt and Howe trusses?
o: Their diagonals slope in opposite directions
Only one of them has vertical members
One of them has no diagonal members
They differ only in roof covering
questions.ref: AISC, Design Guide / structural-steel terminology for Pratt, Howe and Warren truss configurations
questions.n: Pratt and Howe trusses use related vertical/diagonal layouts but reverse the diagonal orientation and typical force roles.

questions.q: What is an opening through a parapet that allows water to drain from a flat roof?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - roofing, roof-framing and sheet-metal terminology
questions.n: A scupper is an opening through a parapet or wall used to drain roof water.

questions.q: What internal intersection is formed where two sloping roof planes meet and direct water toward the low point?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - roof framing, sheathing, underlayment, eaves, rakes and drainage
questions.n: A valley is the internal angle formed by the intersection of two sloping roof planes.

questions.q: Two roofing sheets provide nominal lengths of 3.60 m and 2.70 m with a 0.30 m end lap. What effective slope length do they cover?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Roofing Materials, corrugated G.I. sheet estimating and Table 6-2
questions.n: The overlap is counted only once, so effective coverage is 3.60+2.70−0.30=6.00 m.

questions.q: How many total sheets are required when each of the 20 roof positions uses one 12 ft sheet and one 9 ft sheet?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Roofing Materials, corrugated G.I. sheet estimating and Table 6-2
questions.n: There are 20 sheet positions across the roof and two lengths are needed in each position.
questions.scenario: A roof slope is 6.00 m long and the gutter line 14.00 m. Corrugated GI sheets have a 0.70 m effective width and a 0.30 m end lap; each run uses one 12 ft (3.60 m) and one 9 ft (2.70 m) sheet. Rivets: 26 per 12 ft sheet, 22 per 9 ft sheet.

questions.q: A roof edge slopes upward along the end wall of a gable. What is that edge called?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - roof framing, sheathing, underlayment, eaves, rakes and drainage
questions.n: The sloping edge at the gable end is the rake.

questions.q: For corrugated G.I. roofing with a 1½-corrugation side lap, what effective width is used?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Roofing Materials, corrugated G.I. sheet estimating and Table 6-2
questions.n: Fajardo uses 0.70 m effective width for 1½-corrugation side laps.

questions.q: Which truss uses a repeating series of alternating diagonal members that form triangular panels?
questions.ref: AISC, Design Guide / structural-steel terminology for Pratt, Howe and Warren truss configurations
questions.n: A Warren truss is identified by alternating diagonals forming a triangular or sawtooth web pattern.

questions.q: What short rafter runs perpendicular to the main rafters to support a rake overhang?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - roofing, roof-framing and sheet-metal terminology
questions.n: A lookout is a short framing member that projects or runs perpendicular to support a rake/fly-rafter overhang.

questions.q: What is the lower horizontal edge of a sloping roof that projects beyond the wall called?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - roof framing, sheathing, underlayment, eaves, rakes and drainage
questions.n: The eave is the lower roof edge, commonly projecting beyond the exterior wall.

questions.q: Using 26 rivets for each 12 ft sheet and 22 for each 9 ft sheet, how many rivets are required?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Roofing Materials, corrugated G.I. sheet estimating and Table 6-2
questions.n: Twenty 12 ft sheets require 520 rivets and twenty 9 ft sheets require 440 rivets, for a total of 960.
questions.scenario: A roof slope is 6.00 m long and the gutter line 14.00 m. Corrugated GI sheets have a 0.70 m effective width and a 0.30 m end lap; each run uses one 12 ft (3.60 m) and one 9 ft (2.70 m) sheet. Rivets: 26 per 12 ft sheet, 22 per 9 ft sheet.

questions.q: Rainwater on a flat roof reaches a rectangular opening cut through the parapet. Which drainage component is being described?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - roofing, roof-framing and sheet-metal terminology
questions.n: A parapet opening that drains roof water is a scupper.

questions.q: What end lap is standard for corrugated GI roofing sheets?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Roofing Materials, corrugated G.I. sheet estimating and Table 6-2
questions.n: Common practice uses a standard end-lap range of approximately 25–30 cm.

questions.q: In a conventional Howe truss under gravity loading, which members are characteristically in compression?
questions.ref: AISC, Design Guide / structural-steel terminology for Pratt, Howe and Warren truss configurations
questions.n: The characteristic Howe arrangement has diagonal members generally acting in compression under balanced gravity loading.

questions.q: What is the principal function of roof sheathing?
o: A vapor coating on the purlins
A continuous deck under the roofing
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - roof framing, sheathing, underlayment, eaves, rakes and drainage
questions.n: Roof sheathing spans and braces framing while providing a continuous base for roofing materials.

questions.q: What is the sloping edge of a roof at a gable end called?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - roof framing, sheathing, underlayment, eaves, rakes and drainage
questions.n: A rake is the inclined edge of a roof at a gable end.

questions.q: Purlins are spaced 0.60 m on center along a 6.00 m slope, with one at each end. How many purlin lines are needed?
questions.ref: Roofing estimates
questions.n: Lines = spaces + 1.

questions.q: How many roofing sheets are required across one row along the 14.00 m gutter line?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Roofing Materials, corrugated G.I. sheet estimating and Table 6-2
questions.n: At 0.70 m effective width per sheet, 14.00 m requires exactly 20 sheets in each row.
questions.scenario: A roof slope is 6.00 m long and the gutter line 14.00 m. Corrugated GI sheets have a 0.70 m effective width and a 0.30 m end lap; each run uses one 12 ft (3.60 m) and one 9 ft (2.70 m) sheet. Rivets: 26 per 12 ft sheet, 22 per 9 ft sheet.

questions.q: Why are longer commercially available roof sheets generally preferred when practical?
o: They remove the need for fasteners
They reduce the number of end laps
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Roofing Materials, corrugated G.I. sheet estimating and Table 6-2
questions.n: Fewer end laps reduce overlap waste and simplify installation.

questions.q: In a conventional Pratt truss under gravity loading, which web members are characteristically in tension?
questions.ref: AISC, Design Guide / structural-steel terminology for Pratt, Howe and Warren truss configurations
questions.n: The characteristic Pratt arrangement reverses the Howe web-force pattern: diagonals generally act in tension under balanced gravity loading.

questions.q: What is the primary role of roof underlayment beneath the finished roof covering?
o: To carry all roof dead load directly
To provide a secondary weather-resistive layer
To act as the main structural framing
questions.ref: National Roofing Contractors Association (NRCA) Roofing Manual - roof membranes, underlayments and drainage terminology
questions.n: Underlayment provides supplemental water-shedding/weather protection beneath the primary roof covering.

questions.q: What line is formed where two roof planes meet at the highest point?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - roof framing, sheathing, underlayment, eaves, rakes and drainage
questions.n: A ridge is the horizontal line at the upper intersection of two sloping roof planes.

questions.q: A 10.50 m gutter line uses corrugated sheets with 0.70 m effective width. How many sheets are needed in one row?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Roofing Materials, corrugated G.I. sheet estimating and Table 6-2

questions.q: Which pair of commercial sheet lengths covers the 6.00 m slope while allowing a 0.30 m end lap with minimal excess?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Roofing Materials, corrugated G.I. sheet estimating and Table 6-2
questions.n: A 12 ft sheet is about 3.60 m and a 9 ft sheet about 2.70 m. Their combined nominal length is 6.30 m; subtracting the 0.30 m lap gives 6.00 m effective coverage.
questions.scenario: A roof slope is 6.00 m long and the gutter line 14.00 m. Corrugated GI sheets have a 0.70 m effective width and a 0.30 m end lap; each run uses one 12 ft (3.60 m) and one 9 ft (2.70 m) sheet. Rivets: 26 per 12 ft sheet, 22 per 9 ft sheet.
